beats.en: Start with 1,000 and keep adding a thousand: 1,000, 2,000, 3,000 and so on up to 9,000. Add one more thousand and we get ten thousand, written 10,000.

textbookBox.concept: Our place value chart gets one more column. From the right the columns are Ones, Tens, Hundreds, Thousands and now Ten Thousands, written TTh. Each column is worth ten times the one on its right.

beats.en: Our place value chart gets one more column. From the right the columns are Ones, Tens, Hundreds, Thousands and now Ten Thousands, written TTh. Each column is worth ten times the one on its right.

beats.en: So 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tens make 1 hundred, 10 hundreds make 1 thousand and 10 thousands make 1 ten thousand.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 5 maths · We the Travellers (I) · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: We use the same ten digits, 0 to 9, in every place. For example 1,380 is 1 thousand, 3 hundreds, 8 tens and 0 ones. And 9,123 is 9 thousands, 1 hundred, 2 tens and 3 ones.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from We the Travellers (I): We use the same ten digits, 0 to 9, in every place. For example 1,380 is 1 thousand, 3 hundreds, 8 tens and 0 ones. And 9,123 is 9 thousands, 1 hundred, 2 tens and 3 ones.
